arXiv:0902.3073v1 [math.CA] 18 Feb 2009

Log-convexity and log-concavity of hypergeometric-like functions

D. Karp    S.M. Sitnik

Abstract. We find sufficient conditions for log-convexity and log-concavity for the functions of the forms a↦∑fk​(a)k​xka\mapsto\sum{f_{k}}(a)_{k}x^{k}, a↦∑fk​Γ​(a+k)​xka\mapsto\sum{f_{k}}\Gamma(a+k)x^{k} and a↦∑fk​xk/(a)ka\mapsto\sum{f_{k}}x^{k}/(a)_{k}. The most useful examples of such functions are generalized hypergeometric functions. In particular, we generalize the Turán inequality for the confluent hypergeometric function recently proved by Barnard, Gordy and Richards and log-convexity results for the same function recently proved by Baricz. Besides, we establish a reverse inequality which complements naturally the inequality of Barnard, Gordy and Richards. Similar results are established for the Gauss and the generalized hypergeometric functions. A conjecture about monotonicity of a quotient of products of confluent hypergeometric functions is made.

Keywords: Hypergeometric function, Kummer function, Gauss function, log-convexity, log-concavity, Turán inequality

MSC2000: 26A51, 33C20, 33C15, 33C05

1. Introduction.

This paper is motivated by some recent results dealing with log-convexity and log-concavity of hypergeometric functions as functions of parameters. More specifically, Baricz showed in [Baricz1] that the Kummer function (or the confluent hypergeometric function)

F11​(a,c,x)=∑k=0∞(a)k(c)k​xkk!,{{}_{1}F_{1}}(a;c;x)=\sum\limits_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(a)_{k}}{(c)_{k}}\frac{x^{k}}{k!}, (1)

where (a)k=a(a+1)⋯(a+k−1)=Γ(a+k)/Γ(a)(a)_{k}=a(a+1)\cdots(a+k-1)=\Gamma(a+k)/\Gamma(a) is Pochhammer’s symbol, is log-convex in cc on (0,∞)(0,\infty) for a,x>0a,x>0 as well as the function μ↦F11​(a+μ,c+μ,x)\mu\mapsto{{}_{1}F_{1}}(a+\mu;c+\mu;x) on [0,∞)[0,\infty). This implies, in particular, the reverse Turán type inequality

F11​(a,c+1,x)2≤F11​(a,c,x)​F11​(a,c+2,x).{{}_{1}F_{1}}(a;c+1;x)^{2}\leq{{}_{1}F_{1}}(a;c;x){{}_{1}F_{1}}(a;c+2;x). (2)

(This sort of inequalities are called ”Turán type“ after Paul Turán in a 1946 letter to Szegő proved the inequality [Pn​(x)]2>Pn−1​(x)​Pn+1​(x)[P_{n}(x)]^{2}>P_{n-1}(x)P_{n+1}(x), −1<x<1-1<x<1, for Legendre polynomials PnP_{n}, which has a similar look as (2) but different nature (see [Szegő]).) Baricz’s other results [Baricz2, Baricz3] deal with log-convexity and some more general comparisons of means for the Bessel functions (expressible in terms of F10{{}_{0}F_{1}}) and the Gauss function F12{{}_{2}F_{1}}. Many of his proofs hinge on the additivity of concavity and logarithmic convexity. This method does not work, however, for proving logarithmic concavity since in general it is not additive.

Closely related results were given a bit earlier by Ismail and Laforgia in [Ismail-Laforgia]. In particular, they showed that the determinant

Dn​(x)=|h⁡(a,c,x)h⁡(a,c+1,x)⋯h⁡(a,c+n,x)h⁡(a,c+1,x)h⁡(a,c+2,x)⋯h⁡(a,c+n+1,x)h⁡(a,c+n,x)h⁡(a,c+n+1,x)⋯h⁡(a,c+n,x)|,D_{n}(x)=\begin{vmatrix}h(a,c,x)&h(a,c+1,x)&\cdots&h(a,c+n,x)\\ h(a,c+1,x)&h(a,c+2,x)&\cdots&h(a,c+n+1,x)\\ \vdots&\vdots&&\vdots\\ h(a,c+n,x)&h(a,c+n+1,x)&\cdots&h(a,c+n,x)\end{vmatrix},

where h⁡(a,c,x)=Γ⁡(c−a)​F11​(a,c,x)/Γ⁡(c)h(a,c,x)=\Gamma(c-a){{}_{1}F_{1}}(a;c;x)/\Gamma(c), has positive power series coefficients. For n=1n=1 this leads to an inequality which is weaker than (2).

Carey and Gordy conjectured in [CG] that the Turán type inequality

[F11​(a,c,x)]2>F11​(a+1,c,x)​F11​(a−1,c,x),[{{}_{1}F_{1}}(a;c;x)]^{2}>{{}_{1}F_{1}}(a+1;c;x){{}_{1}F_{1}}(a-1;c;x),

holds for a>0a>0, c>a+2c>{a+2}, x>0x>{0}. Using a clever combination of contiguous relations and telescoping sums Barnard, Gordy and Richards have recently shown in [BGR] that this is indeed true and even more general inequality

[F11​(a,c,x)]2≥F11​(a+ν,c,x)​F11​(a−ν,c,x)[{{}_{1}F_{1}}(a;c;x)]^{2}\geq{{}_{1}F_{1}}(a+\nu;c;x){{}_{1}F_{1}}(a-\nu;c;x) (3)

holds for a>0a>0, c>a≥ν−1c>a\geq\nu-1 and x∈𝐑x\in{\mathbf{R}} or a≥ν−1a\geq\nu-1, c>−1c>-1 (c≠0c\neq{0}), x>0x>0, and positive integer ν\nu. In fact, the authors show that the difference of the left-hand and the right-hand sides of (3) has positive power series coefficients for a>0a>0, a≥ν−1a\geq\nu-1, c>−1c>-1. They also indicate that a similar result is true for the generalized hypergeometric function

Fqp((ap);(bq);x)=Fqp((ap)(bq)|x)=∑n=0∞(a1)n(a2)n⋯(ap)n(b1)n⋯(bq)nn!xn{{}_{p}F_{q}}\left((a_{p});(b_{q});x\right)={{}_{p}F_{q}}\left(\left.\!\!\begin{array}[]{c}(a_{p})\\ (b_{q})\end{array}\right|x\!\right)=\sum\limits_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(a_{1})_{n}(a_{2})_{n}\cdots(a_{p})_{n}}{(b_{1})_{n}\cdots(b_{q})_{n}n!}x^{n} (4)

if p≤q+1p\leq{q+1}, ai>bia_{i}>b_{i}, i=2,…,pi=2,\ldots,p and bi>0b_{i}>0, i=1,…,qi=1,\ldots,q.

In this paper we shall demonstrate that log-convexity and log-concavity properties of hypergeometric functions in their upper and lower parameters serve as an illustration of a more general phenomenon. Namely, we give sufficient conditions for the function x↦f⁡(a+δ,x)​f​(b,x)−f⁡(b+δ,x)​f​(a,x)x\mapsto{f(a+\delta,x)f(b,x)-f(b+\delta,x)f(a,x)} to have positive power series coefficients if f⁡(a,x)=∑fk​(a)k​xkf(a,x)=\sum f_{k}(a)_{k}x^{k}, f⁡(a,x)=∑fk​Γ​(a+k)​xkf(a,x)=\sum f_{k}\Gamma(a+k)x^{k} or f⁡(a,x)=∑fk​xk/(a)kf(a,x)=\sum f_{k}x^{k}/(a)_{k}, where fk>0f_{k}>0 for all kk. Log-convexity or log-concavity then follow immediately. Section 2 of the paper contains three general theorems for these three types of functions and a corollary which includes direct and reverse Turán type inequalities. Section 3 collects some applications to hypergeometric functions. In particular, we extend the result Barnard, Gordy and Richards (3) to non-integer positive ν\nu and complement it with a reverse inequality giving asymptotically precise lower bound for the quantity

F11​(a+ν,c,x)​F11​(a−ν,c,x)[F11​(a,c,x)]2\frac{{{}_{1}F_{1}}(a+\nu;c;x){{}_{1}F_{1}}(a-\nu;c;x)}{[{{}_{1}F_{1}}(a;c;x)]^{2}}

bounded by 11 from above according to (3). We also extend some results of Baricz and provide sufficient conditions for log-concavity and log-convexity of the generalized hypergeometric functions which are less restrictive then the conditions ai>bia_{i}>b_{i} for the (less general) Turán type inequality given in [BGR]. We use the generalized Stieltjes transform representation for Fqq+1{{}_{q+1}F_{q}} from [KarpSitnik] to extend this results to negative xx. One curious corollary of these results is positivity of certain finite hypergeometric sums evaluated at −1-1.

We note in passing the the true Turán type inequalities for the classical orthogonal polynomials [Gasper, Szegő] have been also shown to exemplify a more general phenomenon. Namely, it has been demonstrated in [Szwarc] that they are dependent on certain monotonicity properties of the coefficients of three-term recurrence relations. See further development in [BergSzwarc].

2. General theorems.

A function f:[a,b]↦𝐑f:[a,b]\mapsto{\mathbf{R}} is said to be Wright-convex (strictly Wright-convex) if Fh​(x)=f⁡(x+h)−f⁡(x)F_{h}(x)=f(x+h)-f(x) is non-decreasing (increasing) on [a,b−h][a,b-h] for any fixed h>0h>0. If Fh​(x)F_{h}(x) is non-increasing (decreasing) then ff is Wright-concave (strictly Wright-concave). This notion was introduced by Wright in the 1950s and well studied (see [DragomirPearce, p.246] and [MPF, p.3]). Clearly, Wright-convexity implies mid-point convexity and it can be shown (see [MPF, p.2]) that convexity implies Wright-convexity so that by the celebrated result of Jensen (see, for instance, [Niculescu-Persson, Theorem 1.1.4]) for continuous functions all three notions (convexity, Wright-convexity and mid-point convexity) are equivalent. In general the inclusions Convex⊂\,\subset\,Wright-convex⊂\,\subset\,Midpoint convex are proper. We only deal here with log-convexity (log-concavity) of continuous functions so for our purposes we record

  Proposition 1

Suppose f:[a,b]↦𝐑f:[a,b]\mapsto\mathbf{R} is continuous and has constant sign. Then ff is log-convex (strictly log-convex) iff x↦f⁡(x+h)/f⁡(x)x\mapsto{f(x+h)/f(x)} is non-decreasing (increasing) on [a,b−h][a,b-h] for each fixed h>0h>0 and ff is log-concave (strictly log-concave) iff x↦f⁡(x+h)/f⁡(x)x\mapsto{f(x+h)/f(x)} is non-increasing (decreasing) on [a,b−h][a,b-h] for each fixed h>0h>0.

Using Proposition 1 we will formulate our results in terms of more common log-convexity (log-concavity) while if fact we prove Wright log-convexity (log-concavity).

In what follows in this section the power series expansions are understood as formal, so that no questions of convergence are discussed. It is usually clear in specific applications which variable range should be considered. We will use the standard notation (a)n=a(a+1)⋯(a+n−1)(a)_{n}=a(a+1)\cdots(a+n-1) for the shifted factorial or the Pochhammer symbol. The main idea in the proof of the next theorem belongs to Fedor Nazarov (University of Wisconsin).

f⁡(a,x)=∑n=0∞fn​(a)nn!​xn,f(a,x)=\sum\limits_{n=0}^{\infty}f_{n}\frac{(a)_{n}}{n!}x^{n}, (5)

g⁡(a,x)=∑n=0∞gn​Γ​(a+n)​xn,g(a,x)=\sum\limits_{n=0}^{\infty}g_{n}\Gamma(a+n)x^{n},

  Corollary 1

Let f⁡(a,x)f(a,x) be given by (5) with decreasing sequence {fn/fn−1}\{f_{n}/f_{n-1}\}, then for b>a>0b>a>0 and x>0x>0

with

because x↦(x+α)/(x+β)x\mapsto(x+\alpha)/(x+\beta), α>β≥0\alpha>\beta\geq{0}, is decreasing for x>0x>0. Further for k<m−kk<m-k we have the inequalities

3. Applications to hypergeometric functions

First consider the Kummer function (1). For a,c>0a,c>0 it satisfies the conditions of Theorem 1 with fn=1/(c)nf_{n}=1/(c)_{n} and conditions of Theorem 3 with hn=(a)n/n!h_{n}=(a)_{n}/n!. Besides, Γ⁡(a)​F11​(a,c,x)\Gamma(a){{}_{1}F_{1}}(a;c;x) satisfies the conditions of Theorem 2 with gn=1/[(c)n​n!]g_{n}=1/[(c)_{n}n!]. Clearly, fn/fn−1=1/(c+n−1)f_{n}/f_{n-1}=1/(c+n-1) is decreasing and we are also in the position to apply Corollary 1. Using the Kummer transformation F11​(a,c,x)=e−x​F11​(c−a,c,−x){{}_{1}F_{1}}(a;c;x)=e^{-x}{{}_{1}F_{1}}(c-a;c;-x) we can extend some of the results to negative xx. We collect the consequences of the general theorems for the Kummer function in the following two statements.

for a<b<c−δa<b<c-\delta and c>0>xc>0>x

Numerical tests suggests that the following enhancement of Theorem 4 c) is true:

Conjecture. The ratio in the middle of (10) is monotone decreasing from (0,∞)(0,\infty) onto (1,A)(1,A), where AA is the left-hand side of (10); the ratio in the middle of (11) is monotone increasing from (−∞,0)(-\infty,0) onto (B,1)(B,1), where BB is the left-hand side of (11).

anbn≥an−1bn−1≥⋯≥a1b1≥a0b0\frac{a_{n}}{b_{n}}\geq\frac{a_{n-1}}{b_{n-1}}\geq\cdots\geq\frac{a_{1}}{b_{1}}\geq\frac{a_{0}}{b_{0}} (14)

and non-positive coefficients if

anbn≤an−1bn−1≤⋯≤a1b1≤a0b0.\frac{a_{n}}{b_{n}}\leq\frac{a_{n-1}}{b_{n-1}}\leq\cdots\leq\frac{a_{1}}{b_{1}}\leq\frac{a_{0}}{b_{0}}. (15)

If AA and BB are not identical then some of the coefficients are positive under (14) (so that A′​(x)​B​(x)−B′​(x)​A​(x)>0A^{\prime}(x)B(x)-B^{\prime}(x)A(x)>0 for x>0x>0) and negative under (15) (so that A′​(x)​B​(x)−B′​(x)​A​(x)<0A^{\prime}(x)B(x)-B^{\prime}(x)A(x)<0 for x>0x>0).

Proof. We have

A′​(x)​B​(x)−B′​(x)​A​(x)=∑k=1n∑i=0nk​ak​bi​xi+k−1−∑k=1n∑i=0nk​bk​ai​xi+k−1A^{\prime}(x)B(x)-B^{\prime}(x)A(x)=\sum\limits_{k=1}^{n}\sum\limits_{i=0}^{n}ka_{k}b_{i}x^{i+k-1}-\sum\limits_{k=1}^{n}\sum\limits_{i=0}^{n}kb_{k}a_{i}x^{i+k-1}
=1x​∑k=1n∑i=0nxi+k​k​(ak​bi−ai​bk)=∑m=12​nxm−1​∑i+k=mi≥0,k≥1k,i≤nk⁡(ak​bi−ai​bk)=\frac{1}{x}\sum\limits_{k=1}^{n}\sum\limits_{i=0}^{n}x^{i+k}k(a_{k}b_{i}-a_{i}b_{k})=\sum\limits_{m=1}^{2n}x^{m-1}\sum\limits_{\begin{subarray}{c}i+k=m\\ i\geq{0},k\geq{1}\end{subarray}}^{k,i\leq{n}}k(a_{k}b_{i}-a_{i}b_{k})

Since each term in the inner sum with i=ki=k is clearly zero, we may write:

∑i+k=mi≥0,k≥1k,i≤nk⁡(ak​bi−ai​bk)=∑i+k=m,k<ii≥0,k≥1k,i≤nk⁡(ak​bi−ai​bk)+∑i+k=m,k>ii≥0,k≥1k,i≤nk⁡(ak​bi−ai​bk)\sum\limits_{\begin{subarray}{c}i+k=m\\ i\geq{0},k\geq{1}\end{subarray}}^{k,i\leq{n}}k(a_{k}b_{i}-a_{i}b_{k})=\sum\limits_{\begin{subarray}{c}i+k=m,k<i\\ i\geq{0},k\geq{1}\end{subarray}}^{k,i\leq{n}}k(a_{k}b_{i}-a_{i}b_{k})+\sum\limits_{\begin{subarray}{c}i+k=m,k>i\\ i\geq{0},k\geq{1}\end{subarray}}^{k,i\leq{n}}k(a_{k}b_{i}-a_{i}b_{k})

Due to condition (14) every term in the second sum is non-negative. For each term in the first sum (say indexed k=k∗k=k^{*}, i=i∗i=i^{*}, k∗<i∗k^{*}<i^{*}), there is a term in the second sum with k=i∗k=i^{*}, i=k∗i=k^{*} and

Since AA and BB are not identical at least one of the inequalities (14) is strict which implies that some of the terms above is strictly positive. The second statement follows from A′​(x)​B​(x)−B′​(x)​A​(x)=−(B′​(x)​A​(x)−A′​(x)​B​(x))A^{\prime}(x)B(x)-B^{\prime}(x)A(x)=-(B^{\prime}(x)A(x)-A^{\prime}(x)B(x)) by exchanging the roles of AA and BB.  □\square

Remark 6. It is easy to verify directly that conditions (14) are also necessary for A′​(x)​B​(x)−B′​(x)​A​(x)>0A^{\prime}(x)B(x)-B^{\prime}(x)A(x)>0 if x>0x>0 when n=1n=1 and n=2n=2 (similarly for conditions (15)).
